You extract source evidence for a paper-derived scientific benchmark. Return exactly one JSON object matching the supplied schema, with no Markdown or additional text.

Use only the fixed, line-numbered source packet. Do not use outside knowledge and do not infer an omitted coefficient, exponent, range, experimental condition, or uncertainty convention.

Extract at most one relation: the best source-supported executable quantitative relation connecting one to five numeric controls to one or two numeric readouts. A second source-reported condition is not required. Do not construct a pair, alternate world, counterfactual, task prompt, or benchmark design. If the source contains no complete relation, return {"relations":[]}.

The relation has exactly six fields: formula, parameters, controls, readouts, domain, and anchors. Formula.outputs is an executable expression tree for the source-reported central relation. Output keys must exactly match the readout names. A var leaf names a declared control and a param leaf names a declared parameter. Every declared control and parameter must occur in the formula. Numeric literals are allowed only for structural zero and one; encode every other scientific constant or fitted value as an anchored parameter. Preserve equality, approximation, fitted-relation, and asymptotic scope through the applicability statements; do not turn proportionality without its coefficient, an inequality, or an unspecified function into an exact point predictor.

A control is a numeric independent variable that can be queried within the source-supported domain. A readout is the quantitative dependent variable returned by the relation. Do not turn a latent quantity or an unreported fitted quantity into a control. Use continuous_interval only when the source supports a finite interval with minimum below maximum. Use numeric_values only for at least two explicitly supported numeric values. The domain must name every control exactly once. Record source-reported applicability or fixed context when present; otherwise use an empty applicability array.

Every formula, parameter value, control definition, readout definition, control domain, and applicability statement must carry direct inclusive source line ranges. Anchors contain line_start and line_end only. Do not generate a paraphrased support field. Use the line coordinates exactly as supplied.

Do not output source identity, schema version, an assessment, readiness flag, mechanisms, claim dependencies, ambiguity records, budget, diagnostic conditions, held-out conditions, public prose, provenance mappings, or code. Source identity and all benchmark-design fields are supplied or generated by deterministic code.

L002439	\begin{abstract}
L002440	  \noindent
L002441	   The time-dependent $C\!P$ asymmetry in $B^{0}\!\to{J\mskip-3mu/\mskip-2mu\psi}\rho(770)^0$ decays is measured using proton-proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $6\,\text{fb}^{-1}$, collected with the LHCb detector at a center-of-mass energy of $13\,\text{Te\kern -0.1em V}$ during the years 2015--2018. The $C\!P$-violation parameters for this process are determined to be $2\beta^{\rm eff}_{c\bar{c}d} = 0.710 \pm 0.084 \pm 0.051\,\text{rad}$ and $|\lambda| = 1.019 \pm 0.034 \pm 0.024$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic. This constitutes the first observation of time-dependent $C\!P$ violation in $B^{0}\!\to{J\mskip-3mu/\mskip-2mu\psi}\rho(770)^0$ decays.
L002442	Assuming approximate SU(3) flavor symmetry, these results are combined with the previous consistent LHCb measurement to set the most stringent constraint on the penguin contribution, $\Delta\phi_{s}$, to the $C\!P$-violating phase $\phi_{s}$ in $B^{0}_{s}\!\to{J\mskip-3mu/\mskip-2mu\psi}\phi(1020)$ decays, yielding $\Delta\phi_{s} = 5.0 \pm 4.6\,\text{mrad}$.
L002443	\end{abstract}

L002520	Studies of $\CP$ violation in $B$ mesons are essential for understanding the matter--antimatter asymmetry in the Universe~\cite{Sakharov:1967dj,PDG2024}. This phenomenon was first observed in $\Bd$ meson by the \babar~\cite{BaBar:2001pki} and \belle~\cite{Belle:2001zzw} experiments. Such measurements play a vital role in testing the Standard Model (SM) and exploring new physics phenomena.
L002521	
L002522	The \CP-violating phase associated with the $\Bs$--$\Bsb$ mixing process, $\phis$, is a key observable sensitive to contributions of new particles in the mixing~\cite{Buras:2009if}. In the SM, its value at tree level is precisely determined by a global fit to experimental data to be ${-37.6}^{+0.6}_{-0.5}\mrad$~\cite{CKMfitter2015}.
L002523	It is measured through the interference between $\Bs$--$\Bsb$ mixing and subsequent decays
L002524	via $\decay{\bquark}{\cquark\cquarkbar\squark}$ transitions, neglecting subleading electroweak-loop (penguin) contributions. Current measurements in the golden decay channel
L002525	$\decay{\Bs}{\jpsi\phi(1020)}$ yield an average value of \mbox{$\phis=-50\pm17\mrad$}~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2023-016,ATLAS:2020lbz,CMS:2024znt},
L002526	with an experimental uncertainty now comparable to the possible shift, $\Delta\phis$, due to the neglected penguin contamination with a different weak phase from the leading tree amplitude~\cite{Liu:2013nea,DeBruyn:2014oga,Frings:2015eva,Barel:2020jvf,DeBruyn:2025rhk}.
L002527	Thus, a thorough understanding of the penguin effects becomes mandatory for precision tests of the SM.
L002528	
L002529	
L002530	Long-distance nonperturbative effects in $\decay{\Bs}{\jpsi\phi(1020)}$ decays prevent a precise
L002531	theoretical calculation of $\Delta\phis$.
L002532	An estimate of $\Delta\phis$ can be obtained using \CP-violation parameters in $\decay{\bquark}{\cquark\cquarkbar\squark}$ and $\decay{\bquark}{\cquark\cquarkbar\dquark}$ decays employing SU(3) flavor symmetry, assuming that the corresponding ratios of the hadronic amplitudes of the penguin and tree decay topologies are
L002533	identical~\cite{Liu:2013nea,DeBruyn:2014oga,Frings:2015eva,Barel:2020jvf,DeBruyn:2025rhk}.
L002534	The decay $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\rho(770)^0}$, which proceeds via the Cabibbo-suppressed $\decay{\bquark}{\cquark\cquarkbar\dquark}$ transition,
L002535	serves as a control channel due to its enhanced sensitivity to the hadronic parameters of penguin contributions relative to
L002536	$\decay{\Bs}{\jpsi\phi(1020)}$~\cite{Barel:2020jvf}.
L002537	
L002538	The measured \CP-violation parameters in $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\rho(770)^0}$ and $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\KS}$ decays allow for a determination of the penguin contributions in the former, which
L002539	is used to estimate the penguin shift $\Delta\phis$. This estimate was performed by the LHCb collaboration
L002540	using proton-proton ($\pp$) collision data collected in 2011--2012 \mbox{(Run~1)} at center-of-mass energies of $\sqs=7$ and $8\tev$,  corresponding to an integrated luminosity of \mbox{3\invfb}~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-058}.
L002541	The obtained result of $\Delta\phis=0.9\pm9.8\mrad$ remains insufficiently precise to constrain the penguin effects on the $\phis$ measurement.
L002542	This Letter reports an updated study of \CP violation in $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\rho(770)^0}$ decays,
L002543	with $\decay{\jpsi}{\mup\mun}$ and $\decay{\rho(770)^0}{\pip\pim}$, using $\pp$ collision data collected by the \lhcb experiment during 2015--2018 \mbox{(Run~2)},
L002544	corresponding to an integrated luminosity of \mbox{6\invfb} at $\sqs=13\tev$, which leads to
L002545	the first observation of \CP violation in this process. These results are combined with those of the \mbox{Run~1} measurement~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-058} to determine $\Delta\phis$.
L002546	As the analysis procedures for the $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\pip\pim}$ and $\decay{\Bs}{\jpsi\pip\pim}$ decays are similar, this study largely follows the procedures described in Refs.~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-058,LHCb-PAPER-2019-003}.
L002547	
L002548	The \lhcb detector is a single-arm forward spectrometer covering the \mbox{pseudorapidity} range $2<\eta <5$,
L002549	described in detail in Refs.~\cite{LHCb-DP-2008-001,LHCb-DP-2014-002}. Simulated events are generated with
L002550	the software described in Refs.~\cite{Sjostrand:2007gs,*Sjostrand:2006za,LHCb-PROC-2010-056,Lange:2001uf,davidson2015photos}.
L002551	They are tuned to match data-taking conditions and are used to study selection requirements, as well as to model detector acceptance and resolution effect.
L002552	The trigger system performs the online selection~\cite{LHCb-DP-2012-004} via a hardware stage
L002553	with requirements of high transverse momentum of hadrons, followed by a software stage
L002554	using two trigger algorithms based on the muon kinematics and two-muon vertex information.
L002555	Since only the first algorithm requires a large impact parameter significance relative to $\pp$ interaction point (primary vertex),
L002556	the two selections exhibit different efficiency dependencies on the $\Bd$ decay time, decay angles, and the $\pip\pim$ invariant mass. Consequently, these dependencies are studied separately.
L002557	
L002558	The reconstruction and selection of $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi(\mup\mun)\pip\pim}$ candidates, which include contributions from the $\rho(770)^0$ and other resonances in the full $\pip\pim$ invariant-mass spectrum, follow the strategy of Ref.~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2019-003}.
L002559	A boosted decision tree classifier is employed to suppress combinatorial background, using variables with good discriminating power, in particular the fit quality of $\Bd$ decay vertex, as well as the particle-identification information and impact parameter of the pions~\cite{LHCb-DP-2008-001}. This selection improves the signal purity under the $\Bd$ peak, defined as within $\pm20\mevcc$ of the known \Bd mass~\cite{PDG2024}, by approximately a factor of eight.
L002560	Peaking backgrounds due to kaon and proton misidentification from
L002561	$\decay{\Bds}{\jpsi\Kst}$, $\decay{\Lb}{\jpsi\proton{h^{-}}(h=K,\pi)}$, and
L002562	$\decay{\Bu}{\jpsi\Kp}$ decays are
L002563	removed by stringent particle identification and mass requirements, while $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\KS}$ decays are vetoed using the $\pip\pim$ invariant mass.
L002564	The same-sign decays $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\pi^\pm\pi^\pm}$, containing two pions with same charge and selected using the same criteria, are used to study the mass shape of the combinatorial background.
L002565	
L002566	Selected $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\pip\pim}$ candidates in the mass range $[5250, 5500]\mevcc$
L002567	are retained for further analysis.
L002568	The invariant mass of a \Bd candidate, $m(\jpsi\pip\pim)$, is calculated by requiring the \Bd momentum vector
L002569	to point back to the closest primary vertex and constraining the $\mup\mun$ invariant mass to the known \jpsi mass~\cite{PDG2024}.
L002570	An unbinned maximum-likelihood fit to the $m(\jpsi\pip\pim)$ distribution
L002571	is performed to discriminate the signal from background contributions.
L002572	The mass shape of the combinatorial background is described by a fifth-order polynomial function,
L002573	which can account for a dip caused by the veto of the $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\Kst}$ decays. Its parameters are
L002574	shared between the $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\pip\pim}$ and $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\pipm\pipm}$ data samples and
L002575	obtained via a simultaneous fit to both samples.
L002576	
L002577	The \Bd and \Bs peaks are each modeled by the sum of a Hypatia function~\cite{Santos:2013gra} and
L002578	a Gaussian function, where the mass difference between \Bd and \Bs peaks is constrained to its known value~\cite{PDG2024}.
L002579	Partially reconstructed backgrounds from $\decay{\Bs}{\jpsi\etapr}(\rhoz\gamma)$ and $\decay{\Bs}{\jpsi\eta}(\pip\pim\gamma)$ decays
L002580	are included in the fit. Their shapes are modeled using simulations, and their yield ratios relative to the \Bd signal are constrained to the values determined from simulations.
L002581	The resulting fit is shown in \figref{fig_jpsipipi} and is used to estimate the yield of each component under the \Bd peak.
L002582	
L002583	
L002584	A signal sample of approximately $51\,000$ $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\pip\pim}$ decays is obtained. In the subsequent analysis, the residual backgrounds under the $\Bd$ peak are statistically subtracted by injecting events with negative weights, with the total weight matching the corresponding background yield~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2020-045,LHCb-PAPER-2019-003}.
L002585	The combinatorial background is subtracted by using candidates in the mass
L002586	interval $[5312,5332]\mevcc$, while simulated samples are used for the partially reconstructed backgrounds. The small contamination from the tail of the $\decay{\Bs}{\jpsi\pip\pim}$ decays
L002587	is subtracted using an amplitude-corrected simulation sample~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2019-003}.

L002602	
L002603	The measurement of \CP violation in $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\pip\pim}$ decays requires an amplitude analysis to separate different polarization components.
L002604	A weighted multidimensional maximum-likelihood fit is performed to the background-subtracted distributions of the decay time,
L002605	the invariant mass $m(\pip\pim)$, and the angular variables $(\cospi, \cosmu, \chi)$.
L002606	The helicity angle \thepi (\themu) is defined as the angle between the \pip (\mup) momentum and the
L002607	direction opposite to the $\Bd$ momentum in the $\pip\pim(\mup\mun)$ rest frame,
L002608	and $\chi$ is the azimuthal angle between the $\pip\pim$ and $\mumu$ decay planes~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-058,LHCb-PAPER-2020-042}.
L002609	
L002610	
L002611	The fit is performed simultaneously across six subsamples, categorized by data-taking period and trigger category,
L002612	with a common set of physics parameters.
L002613	The signal probability density function (PDF) in each subsample closely follows the formalism detailed in Refs.~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2019-003,Zhang:2012zk}.
L002614	It incorporates the effects of flavor tagging, decay-time resolution, decay-time and angular detection efficiencies,
L002615	and also considers the contributions of the intermediate resonances to the $m(\pip\pim)$ spectrum.
L002616	The PDF is convolved with a Gaussian function whose
L002617	width is taken as the per-candidate decay-time uncertainty, derived from the uncertainties of the measured momentum and decay distance of $\Bd$ mesons and calibrated using control samples.
L002618	The average decay-time resolution for signal candidates is determined to be $41\,\text{fs}$, which is significantly smaller
L002619	than the $\Bd$ oscillation period and has a negligible impact on the measurement.
L002620	
L002621	
L002622	The acceptance, the reconstruction and the selection generate a nonuniform efficiency as a function of the $\Bd$ decay time, decay angles, and the invariant $\pip\pim$ mass.
L002623	In the following, the efficiency related to the decay angles and the invariant $\pip\pim$ mass is generically denoted as angular efficiency, and it is assumed to be independent of that of the decay time.
L002624	A four-dimensional angular efficiency
L002625	is parametrized by a combination of Legendre and spherical harmonic moments~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2019-003},
L002626	using simulated signal candidates kinematically corrected to match data.
L002627	
L002628	The decay-time efficiency is determined with a well-established data-driven method~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2019-003,LHCb-PAPER-2019-013}, using the control channel $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\Kstarz}$, which is topologically similar to the signal decay. The decay-time efficiency is modeled by a cubic spline function, determined from the decay-time
L002629	distribution of selected candidates divided by that of generated candidates,
L002630	where the latter decay-time distribution is modeled by an exponential distribution with the \Bd lifetime fixed to its known value~\cite{PDG2024},
L002631	convolved with a Gaussian resolution function whose parameters are determined from the resolution study described above.
L002632	The kinematic differences between signal and control modes are corrected using the corresponding simulated samples.
L002633	
L002634	
L002635	The flavor of the \Bd meson at production is identified with two independent flavor-tagging algorithms,
L002636	the opposite-side (OS) tagger~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2011-027} and same-side (SS) tagger~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2016-039}.
L002637	Both methods provide a tagging decision $Q$ and an imperfectly estimated mistag probability $\kappa$ for each \Bd meson.
L002638	The decision $Q$ takes values of $+1$, $-1$, or $0$, corresponding to classifications as \Bd, \Bdb, or untagged, respectively.
L002639	The calibration of the mistag probability $\omega(\kappa)$ follows the strategy in Ref.~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2019-003},
L002640	using a linear function for each algorithm. The OS calibration is performed using $\decay{\Bu}{\jpsi\Kp}$ decays,
L002641	with $\omega$ determined from the number of correct and wrong tagging decisions.
L002642	The SS calibration employs $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\Kstarz}$ decays,
L002643	whose flavors at decay are determined by the charge of final states,
L002644	and $\omega$ is estimated by fitting the decay-time distribution.
L002645	The SS tagging algorithm is trained on samples whose selection biases the decay time and decay angles~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2016-039}, resulting in different
L002646	detection efficiencies for tagged and untagged candidates.
L002647	The effective tagging power, defined as $\epsilon_{\rm tag}(1-2\omega)^2$ with $\epsilon_{\rm tag}$ being the tagging efficiency, is measured to be $4.5\%$ for the combined OS and SS taggers in the full \mbox{Run~2} dataset.
L002648	To simplify the analysis, untagged candidates representing 12\% of the signal are excluded in the fit as they are insensitive to the \CP violation.
L002649	
L002650	
L002651	The $m(\pip\pim)$ spectrum is modeled with six resonances, using the same configuration of amplitude magnitudes and relative phases for each polarization component as in Ref.~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-058}. The $f_0(500)$ resonance is modeled using a Bugg function, with its parameters fixed to the values of the solution (iii) proposed in Ref.~\cite{Bugg:2006gc}.
L002652	The $f_0(1270)$ and $\omega(782)$ resonances are described by relativistic Breit--Wigner (RBW) functions~\cite{PDG2024}, while the $\rho(770)^0$, $\rho(1450)^0$ and $\rho(1700)^0$ resonances are described by Gounaris--Sakurai functions~\cite{Gounaris:1968mw}.
L002653	Their pole masses and decay widths are constrained to the world-average values~\cite{PDG2024}.
L002654	The $\rho(770)^0$ resonance has an independent set of \CP-violation parameters $2\betaeff$ and $\abs{\lambda}$,
L002655	while all the other resonances share another common set.
L002656	The mass difference, decay width and decay width difference of \Bd mass eigenstates,
L002657	as well as the \Bd production asymmetry are shared across all the resonances.
L002658	Among these, the first two parameters are constrained to their
L002659	known values~\cite{PDG2024}, while the latter two are fixed to zero.
L002660	This study reports two fits, where the parameters $2\betaeff$ and $\abs{\lambda}$ are either identical or not across all polarization amplitudes ($A_i$, $i=0,\perp,\parallel$), which are
L002661	defined in the transversity basis~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-058,Zhang:2012zk}. The polarization-independent
L002662	fit is used later to constrain $\Delta\phis$, while the polarization-dependent one accounts for potential differences in the hadronization dynamics among the polarization states.
L002663	The decay-time resolution parameters, as well as the coefficients of the angular and decay-time efficiencies,
L002664	are fixed in the fit, while the flavor-tagging parameters are constrained to the calibration results.

L002696	Potential difference in the angular efficiency between simulated samples and data, arising from mismatches in the momenta of final-state particles, is corrected using an iterative fit as detailed in Ref.~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2019-013}.
L002697	The measured \CP-violation parameters are summarized in \tabref{tab_fitres},
L002698	where statistical uncertainties are estimated using the bootstrapping method~\cite{Efron:1979bxm,Langenbruch:2019nwe}.
L002699	This approach allows the uncertainties from the $\jpsi\pip\pim$ mass fit, including the uncertainties on the contribution of the partially reconstructed background, to be propagated into the statistical uncertainties of the \CP-violation parameters.
L002700	All results are mutually consistent, showing no evidence for a polarization-dependent effect.
L002701	The statistical significance of a nonzero value of 2\betaeff is found to be around ten Gaussian standard deviations using Wilks's theorem~\cite{Wilks:1938dza},
L002702	establishing the first observation of \CP violation in the $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\rho(770)^0}$ decays.
L002703	The corresponding time-dependent \CP asymmetry varies at different points in the phase space, leading to a dilution on this asymmetry.
L002704	To reduce this dilution, a variable $t^{\prime}$, determined as the decay time adjusted by a factor dependent on phase-space position, is used.
L002705	As described in the {\hyperlink{sec_endmatter}{\color{black} End Matter}}, it aligns
L002706	the oscillation phases at different phase-space positions to reduce the dilution on
L002707	the \CP asymmetry. The resulting \CP asymmetry is shown in \figref{fig_bd_fittime}.
L002708	The background-subtracted distributions of $m(\pip\pim)$ and the decay angles, along
L002709	with their fit projections, are shown in \figref{fig_bd_fitamp}.
L002710	As a cross-check, the fit is repeated on subsets of the data, divided by the year of data-taking, magnet polarity, trigger and tagging category.
L002711	In all cases, the obtained results are consistent with the baseline results.

L002743	The total systematic uncertainties reported in \tabref{tab_fitres} are obtained by summing the
L002744	individual contributions in quadrature. These contributions are described below and
L002745	summarized in the {\hyperlink{sec_endmatter}{\color{black} End Matter}}.
L002746	The uncertainties of input parameters constrained in the fit are already incorporated into the
L002747	statistical uncertainties of the fit results.
L002748	The impact of the decay-time resolution is found to be
L002749	negligible on the fit results.
L002750	The systematic uncertainties from the decay width difference and production asymmetry of the \Bd meson are evaluated by varying their values by one
L002751	standard deviation, taken as the quadrature sum of the central values and uncertainties reported by Refs.~\cite{PDG2024} and~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2023-013}, respectively.
L002752	
L002753	Systematic uncertainties related to the $\jpsi\pip\pim$ mass fit model are evaluated by two
L002754	alternative fits using a double-sided Crystal Ball function~\cite{Skwarnicki:1986xj} for
L002755	the signal and a fourth-order polynomial function for the combinatorial background, respectively.
L002756	Potential differences between the sideband candidates used for background subtraction and the true background under the \Bd peak are conservatively accounted for by retaining $20\%$ of the combinatorial background candidates in the fit.
L002757	Systematic uncertainties related to the resonance model are evaluated using RBW functions for the $\rho$ resonances and the Bugg function, with solution (ii) from Ref.~\cite{Bugg:2006gc}, for the $f_0(500)$ resonance.
L002758	The impact of the configuration of \CP-violation parameters is assessed by allowing independent parameters for each resonance in the fit. Alternative fits are performed including either an $f_0(980)$, $f_0(1500)$, $f_0(1700)$, or a nonresonant component, and the maximum observed variations are assigned as systematic uncertainties.
L002759	
L002760	
L002761	Systematic uncertainties from the correction of the simulated samples in the determination of the angular efficiency are evaluated by changing the variables used to derive the corrections.
L002762	Conservative systematic uncertainties from the iterative fit procedure are evaluated by comparing the results with and without the iterative correction.
L002763	Untagged candidates, which exhibit different detection efficiencies compared to tagged candidates, are excluded in the baseline fit. However, as tagging information is unavailable in the control samples, untagged candidates are retained in the acceptance studies. An alternative fit that includes the untagged candidates is performed to assess the impact of this effect.
L002764	
L002765	
L002766	Systematic uncertainties due to the limited sizes of the control samples for the angular and decay-time efficiencies are estimated by varying the corresponding coefficients according to their statistical covariance matrices, where the decay-time contribution is found to be negligible.
L002767	Varying the parametrization models of these efficiencies yields negligible changes. The impact of neglecting correlations between the angular and decay-time efficiencies is assessed using pseudoexperiments.
L002768	
L002769	The results in \tabref{tab_fitres} and Ref.~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-058} are consistent. Their combination, performed accounting for the correlations of systematic uncertainties, yields $2\betaeff= 0.718 \pm 0.088\rad$ and
L002770	$\abs{\lambda}= 1.033 \pm 0.035$, with a correlation coefficient of $0.11$.
L002771	A summary of the LHCb measurements of these parameters is shown in \figref{fig_combplot}
L002772	in the {\hyperlink{sec_endmatter}{\color{black} End Matter}}.
L002773	Parametrizing the magnitude and phase of the strong parts of the effective penguin amplitude relative to the tree amplitude as $ae^{i\theta}$ in the $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\rho(770)^0}$ and
L002774	$a^{\prime}e^{i\theta^{\prime}}$ in the $\decay{\Bs}{\jpsi\phi(1020)}$ decays, and assuming these two ratios are identically quantified,
L002775	the penguin shift $\Delta\phis$ can be estimated through~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-058}
L002776	\begin{equation*}
L002777	  \begin{aligned}
L002778	  \label{eqn_peng_phis2}
L002779	  \Delta\phis & = -{\rm arg}\mbracket{
L002780	  \frac{(\lamp{e}^{2i\gamma}-1)+\epsilon(\lamp-1)}
L002781	  {(\lamp{e}^{2i\gamma}-1)+\epsilon(\lamp-1){e}^{2i\gamma}}
L002782	  },
L002783	\end{aligned}
L002784	\end{equation*}
L002785	with
L002786	\begin{equation*}
L002787	  \begin{aligned}
L002788	  \lamp & \equiv \abs{\lambda}e^{-i(2\betaeff-2\betaccs)}
L002789	        = \frac{1-ae^{i\theta}e^{-i\gamma}}{1-ae^{i\theta}e^{i\gamma}},
L002790	  \end{aligned}
L002791	\end{equation*}
L002792	where $\epsilon=\nu^2/(1-\nu^2)$ is the Cabibbo-suppression factor~\cite{Barel:2020jvf}.
L002793	The Wolfenstein parameter $\nu=0.22501 \pm 0.00068$
L002794	and the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) angle $\gamma=(65.7\pm3.0)\degrees$ are taken from Ref.~\cite{PDG2024},
L002795	and the \CP-violating phase $2\betaccs$ from measurements of $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\KS}$ decays~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2023-013}.
L002796	The penguin contribution $\Delta\phis$ is determined to be $\ValDphis\mrad$,
L002797	with an uncertainty significantly smaller than the current precision on $\phis$.
L002798	A study of SU(3) flavor symmetry breaking is performed by simultaneously scanning the amplitude magnitude ratio $a/a^{\prime}$
L002799	in the range $[0.5, 1.5]$ and the phase difference \mbox{$\theta\!-\!\theta^{\prime}$} over $[-180, 180]^{\circ}$.
L002800	As shown in the Supplemental Material~\cite{Supplemental_material}, the resulting $\Delta\phis$ values vary within
L002801	the range $[-7.8,7.8]\mrad$ and its corresponding uncertainty increases to at most $6.9\mrad$,
L002802	indicating that the uncertainty induced by the breaking of SU(3) flavor symmetry may exceed the precision of the estimate itself.
L002803	
L002804	In summary, time-dependent \CP violation in $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\rho(770)^0}$ decays is observed for the first time.
L002805	From a time-dependent amplitude analysis of $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\pip\pim}$ decays using the full Run~2 dataset collected by the \lhcb experiment, the \CP-violation parameters in the $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\rho(770)^0}$ process are measured to be
L002806	\mbox{$2\betaeff=0.710 \pm 0.084 \pm 0.051 \rad$} and \mbox{$\abs{\lambda}=1.019 \pm 0.034 \pm 0.024 $}.
L002807	These results are consistent with, and two times more precise than the previous
L002808	measurement~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-058}.
L002809	Using SU(3) flavor symmetry to relate the sizes of the penguin contributions in $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\rho(770)^0}$ and $\decay{\Bs}{\jpsi\phi(1020)}$ decays, and combining the previous
L002810	results in Ref.~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-058}, the most stringent constraint on the penguin contribution is determined to be $\Delta\phis = \ValDphis\mrad$.
L002811	The measured \CP-violation parameters will ultimately provide essential inputs to a global study of $B \to \jpsi X$ decays that aims to
L002812	simultaneously determine the phases $2\beta$ and $\phis$ in the presence of
L002813	penguin pollution~\cite{Barel:2020jvf,DeBruyn:2025rhk}.

L002896	The \CP asymmetry shown in \figref{fig_bd_fittime} is obtained by the following procedure.
L002897	The time-dependent \CP asymmetry in the $\decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\pip\pim}$ decays is described by
L002898	\begin{equation*}
L002899	\label{eqn_tdacp}
L002900	   \frac{\overline{\Gamma}(t)-\Gamma(t)}{\overline{\Gamma}(t)+\Gamma(t)}
L002901	   = S\sin(\dmd\,{t})-C\cos(\dmd\,{t}),
L002902	\end{equation*}
L002903	where $\dmd$ is the mass difference of $\Bd$ mass eigenstates~\cite{PDG2024},
L002904	and $S$ and $C$ are \CP-violation coefficients depending on $(\mpipi,\cosmu,\cospi,\chi)$~\cite{Zhang:2012zk}.
L002905	Since the asymmetry depends on the location in the $(\mpipi,\cosmu,\cospi,\chi)$ phase space, the
L002906	overall asymmetry integrated over the phase space is diluted as $S$ or $C$ changes sign.
L002907	Moreover, it is also diluted by the flavor tagging effects.
L002908	To view the \CP asymmetry, the decay time $t$ is transformed to $t^{\prime} = t + \deriv t(\mpipi,\cosmu,\cospi,\chi)$ using
L002909	\begin{equation*}
L002910	\label{eqn_tdacp_relation}
L002911	\begin{aligned}
L002912		\cos(\dmd\,\deriv t) & = S/\sqrt{S^2+C^2},\quad
L002913	    \sin(\dmd\,\deriv t) & = -C/\sqrt{S^2+C^2}, \\
L002914	\end{aligned}
L002915	\end{equation*}
L002916	where $S$ and $C$ are determined by the fit to data.
L002917	The asymmetry is transformed to a single sine function with positive coefficient
L002918	\begin{equation*}
L002919	\label{eqn_tdacp_trans}
L002920	   \frac{\overline{\Gamma}(t^{\prime})-\Gamma(t^{\prime})}{\overline{\Gamma}(t^{\prime})+\Gamma(t^{\prime})}
L002921	   = \sqrt{\mean{S}^2+\mean{C}^2}\sin(\dmd\,{t^{\prime}}),
L002922	\end{equation*}
L002923	where $\mean{S}$ $(\mean{C})$ is the average values of $S$ $(C)$ integrating over the phase space.
L002924	The new asymmetry is not diluted because only positive coefficients are summed, and
L002925	the dilution due to flavor tagging effects still remain.
L002926	The quantity $\dmd\,{t^{\prime}}$ can be in any $2\pi$ period, so $\dmd\,{t^{\prime}}$ is taken to be modulo of $2\pi$.
